claims.text: Retention or loss of toughness in high-entropy alloys is governed by the interaction of lattice strain, dislocation behavior, and nano-twinning.
The relevant high-entropy alloys are random solid solutions.
The relevant alloys have high entropy of mixing.
Lattice strain can be controllably introduced through alloy-composition engineering.
Lattice strain can be controllably introduced through mechanical deformation.
Temperature and dwell time during spark plasma sintering are conditions under which the proposed governing behavior should be evaluated.
Heterogeneous lattice strain causes unusual dislocation behaviors, including multiple kinks or jogs and bidirectional cross-slip.
The unusual dislocation behavior caused by lattice strain produces strengthening mechanisms that underpin a strength-ductility synergy.
Nano-twinning provides an additional deformation mode.
Nano-twinning alleviates the toughness penalty normally associated with high strength.
Optimizing the interaction among lattice strain, dislocation behavior, and nano-twinning will enhance mechanical strength relative to the baseline.
Optimizing the interaction among lattice strain, dislocation behavior, and nano-twinning will enhance toughness relative to the baseline.
The baseline is a conventional high-entropy alloy without deliberately introduced lattice strain or nano-twinning.
The hypothesis is limited to random-solid-solution, high-mixing-entropy alloys processed under varied spark-plasma-sintering temperatures and dwell times.
The exact relationship among lattice strain, dislocation behavior, and nano-twinning is not fully understood.
The hypothesis would be falsified if introduced lattice strain failed to enhance both strength and toughness through altered dislocation behavior and nano-twinning.
